studies.label: In-person pilot of the two-player AUT (GPT, HUM, and CON; randomized within-person session order)

counts_source.locator: PDF p. 3, Figure 1 caption; Section 3.2 describes all participants completing every condition
counts_source.quote: Each participant (N = 62) runs three randomized 4-minute co-creation sessions—once

arms.name: GPT
arms.description: Live GPT-4 partner in a four-minute shared chat, with server-enforced turn-taking and one single-sentence idea per AI turn; the participant then curates the best creative uses. Every participant completed this condition.

arms.name: HUM
arms.description: Live human partner in the same four-minute shared-chat interface, followed by individual curation. Every participant completed this condition. Dyad formation and dependence between partners are not described.

arms.name: CON (pooled)
arms.description: Non-interactive exposure to one of the GPT-generated, highly creative human, or uncreative human seed sets, followed by curation. Every participant completed this condition. This pooled arm includes AI-generated content; other_aid follows the screening form because the schema has no mixed code.

arms.name: CON gpt_con
arms.description: GPT-4-only seed set within CON. Seed-set assignment between participants is not stated to be random; the PDF provides only an approximate subgroup size.

arms.name: CON high_con
arms.description: Highly creative human seed set within CON, selected from Stevenson et al. Seed-set assignment between participants is not stated to be random; the PDF provides only an approximate subgroup size.

arms.name: CON low_con
arms.description: Uncreative human seed set within CON, selected from Stevenson et al. Seed-set assignment between participants is not stated to be random; the PDF provides only an approximate subgroup size.

estimates.outcome: Crowd-rated originality of ideas, GPT partner versus human partner
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality is how unlikely others would be to generate the idea, rated independently by crowdsourced workers on a five-point Likert scale (PDF p. 4, Section 3.4). The analysis uses repeated ratings of ideas. The Figure 1 caption says curated ideas are rated; whether the rated pool also includes partner chat contributions is unresolved.

regression.model: Linear mixed-effects model with fixed effects of partner type, non-interactive seed-set assignment, and their interaction, and random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater (PDF p. 4, Section 4). The companion TOST result is the maximum credible-effect bound |β| ≤ 0.33 (Section 4.1); its test statistic and p-value are not printed.

sources.quote: TOST [15] bounded the maximum credible effect at |β| ≤ 0.33,

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4, mixed-model specification supporting the participant basis of uncertainty
sources.quote: We fit a Linear Mixed-effects Model (LMM) with fixed effects of Partner type, non- interactive assignment, and their interaction, plus random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater.

estimates.notes: Main frequentist specification of the paired GPT-minus-HUM contrast. The coefficient and interval are on the raw originality scale; no standardization is stated. Subject random effects account for repeated observations of each participant, so se_basis is participant despite the rating-level observations. Whether dependence within HUM dyads is also modeled is not stated. Analysis-specific participant counts and rating counts are absent; the overall pilot count is not substituted. No first-round-only estimate is printed. Full-sample arm means and SDs are absent, and the BAS Drive subgroup bars are not combined. The TOST bound is retained in the model description because it is not a point estimate or standard error. The Bayesian record is a re-estimation of this same comparison, not independent evidence.

estimates.outcome: Crowd-rated originality of ideas, GPT partner versus human partner (Bayesian re-estimation)
estimates.question: with_ai
estimates.measure_detail: Originality is how unlikely others would be to generate the idea, rated independently by crowdsourced workers on a five-point Likert scale (PDF p. 4, Section 3.4). The analysis uses repeated ratings of ideas. The Figure 1 caption says curated ideas are rated; whether the rated pool also includes partner chat contributions is unresolved.

regression.model: Bayesian re-estimation of the GPT-minus-HUM originality contrast with a weakly informative Normal(0, 1) prior; coefficient field is the posterior median. The paper does not print a separate Bayesian model formula.

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4.1, Bayesian re-estimation of GPT versus HUM
sources.quote: a Bayesian re-estimation with a weakly informative Normal(0, 1) prior yielded substantial evidence in favor of the null (BF₀₁ = 10.95; posterior median +0.06, 95% credible interval [−0.06, +0.20]).

sources.locator: PDF p. 4, Section 4, model specification; Section 4.1 calls the Bayesian analysis a re-estimation
sources.quote: We fit a Linear Mixed-effects Model (LMM) with fixed effects of Partner type, non- interactive assignment, and their interaction, plus random intercepts for subject, item-within-subject, and rater.

estimates.notes: Alternative Bayesian analysis of the same paired GPT-minus-HUM contrast as s1_novelty_gpt_vs_hum_paired_lmm. regression.coef records the printed posterior median, not a frequentist coefficient estimate; the CI fields hold a Bayesian credible interval, not a sampling confidence interval, and must not be converted into a frequentist SE. test.type other and test.value denote BF₀₁, evidence for the null relative to the alternative, not a t, F, or z statistic. No posterior SD, SE, p-value, or analysis-specific counts are printed. Participant basis follows the paper’s description of this as a re-estimation of the subject-random-intercept model; a separate Bayesian random-effects formula is not printed. Its sign and interval differ from the main frequentist estimate without explanation. Retain as a sensitivity result; do not pool the two specifications as independent observations.

Subgroup and moderation results are excluded. CON pools GPT-generated and human-written seed exposure, so it is not an AI-free control. No arm means, error-bar endpoints, or other figure-only values are read off the graph or combined.

not_extracted.what: S1-O3: originality of CON gpt_con versus CON low_con (seed-quality manipulation check)
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1 describe seed sets assigned between participants, without stating random assignment. not_extracted.what: S1-O3: originality of CON gpt_con versus CON high_con (seed-quality manipulation check)
not_extracted.reason: Seed-set assignment is not stated to be random (PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and Figure 1; PDF p. 6, Section 4.3). The rated texts may be supplied seed ideas rather than participant-produced outputs, so the result may instead be a comparison of AI-only and human-only content.

not_extracted.what: S1-O4: subsequent originality by initial CON seed set, including the omnibus seed-set effect and high_con-versus-gpt_con contrast
not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 6, Section 4.3 restricts this analysis to participants whose first session was CON; the assignment of the seed sets themselves is not described as random. The outcome pools later HUM and GPT sessions, so the printed result also cannot be classified as wholly unassisted after-AI performance.
Defined as practical usefulness, but results are not printed: PDF p. 4, Section 3.4 says, "We report originality here; utility results are available on request."

not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 describes a solo AUT before or after the session loop, but reports no output-scored results or treatment contrast. Assignment to before versus after is not stated to be random.

not_extracted.reason: PDF pp. 4-5, Sections 3.3 and 4.2 and Figure 2 concern participant traits and their associations with originality, including within-person variation. They are not randomized AI-assistance contrasts; within-person variation is not diversity across people.

not_extracted.reason: PDF p. 3, Section 3.2 and PDF p. 5, Section 4.2 analyze self-reported partner perceptions and observational associations with originality. These are self-report or nonrandom predictor analyses, not full-sample randomized AI-assistance contrasts.

open_items: The pilot has a printed overall participant count, but exact participant counts in each mixed-model analysis, per-condition analyzed counts, and the total number of ratings analyzed are absent. n_analyzed and contrast counts remain null; no counts are inferred from degrees of freedom or summed from Figure 3 subgroups.

No full-sample arm means, participant-level SDs, or paired-difference SD/correlation are reported. PDF p. 4, Section 3.4 reports rater-intercept variability; that is not an outcome SD and cannot be used as a standardizer.
No first-round-only GPT-versus-HUM contrast is printed; the extracted results use the paper’s paired analysis.

The rated pool is ambiguous: Figure 1 says curated ideas are rated but also labels the pipeline as ideas generated in chat plus curated. It is unclear whether GPT partner contributions are included in the rated GPT pool.
The PDF does not specify how HUM dyads were formed, whether order randomization operated independently for individuals, or whether the model accounts for dependence between the two human partners.

Seed-set assignment is never called random. The manipulation-check comparison may concern supplied seeds rather than participants’ outputs; neither uncertainty is resolved by randomized order of the partner conditions.
The later-session seed analysis pools HUM and GPT output; separate estimates would be needed to identify an unassisted after-AI outcome.
The Bayesian and frequentist GPT-versus-HUM results have different signs and intervals; the paper does not explain the discrepancy or separately specify the full Bayesian random-effects model.

The document gives inconsistent corpus and rater counts: PDF p. 2, Section 1.1 and Figure 1 report 1,928 ideas, while PDF p. 4, Section 3.4 reports 1,923; the Figure 1 text alternative on PDF p. 4 reports 225 raters, while Section 3.4 reports 226. These are not substituted for contrast-specific counts.
Figure 3 shows unequal BAS Drive subgroup counts across partner conditions without an exclusion explanation. The plotted subgroup means and counts are not used to reconstruct full-sample results.
The model release year and a pilot preregistration are not stated. No preregistered primary outcome can be confirmed.

The citation record identifies a later proceedings version, DOI 10.1145/3803784.3816851. Whether its body changes these results is unverified; this extraction uses only the supplied author-manuscript PDF.
notes: Extraction date: 2026-10-10. Read the entire markdown conversion and all PDF pages, inspected every embedded figure, and checked for tables with pymupdf; no tables, appendix, or supplement were present on file. The numerical inventory for the eligible full-sample comparison comprises the frequentist coefficient, SE, confidence interval and p-value, the TOST bound, and the Bayesian posterior median, credible interval and Bayes factor. Both analysis specifications are preserved as records of the same contrast; the frequentist LMM is the main specification for any primary-record decision. The sample is shared across these records and all partner conditions. No separate diversity outcome is reported. Counts and missing arm summaries were not reconstructed, and no effects or standard errors were calculated. The seed materials cited from Stevenson et al. do not establish shared participants; the screening form reports no other paper using this sample.
